MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Knowledge of the concepts, principles, techniques and procedures of operating an Auto Skills Center or similar facility. Knowledge of tools required for basic vehicle repair. Skill in providing customer service based functions. Skill in performing or advising on basic vehicle repair. Skill in the use of Microsoft Office Programs (e.g., Word, Excel, Power Point, Outlook) and other operating systems used in the program area. Ability to conduct vehicle safety inspections. Ability to operate a cash register in accordance with proper cash handling and Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard procedures (DCI-PSS). Ability to work independently and make sound decisions. Ability to analyze and prepare clear, concise, and technically sound reports related to work within the Division. Ability to market the program and motivate eligible participants. Ability to develop and/or effectively deliver instructional classes and/or training. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.

Details.JobSummary: This position is assigned to the Community Recreation Division; Morale, Welfare and Recreation (MWR) Department; Commander, Navy Region Europe, Africa, Central; Naval Support Activity Souda Bay, Greece. The purpose of this position is to provide day to day management and oversight of the Auto Skills program and services
Details.SubAgencyName: Commander Navy Region Europe, Africa, Central, Naval Support Activity, Souda Bay, Greece.
MajorDuties: Oversees day to day operations of the Auto Skills Center. Monitors the Auto Skills Center program to ensure Navy Program standards are met or exceeded. Conducts vehicle safety inspections on personal vehicles and reports results to the installation Vehicle Control Center (VCC). Assists customers with tool check out and instruction on use of various equipment related to auto repair. Ensures all check-out forms are properly completed and tools are inspected upon return. Collects fees from customers and uses a point of sale (POS) system or other computer program. Administers safety tests before customers use the Auto Skills Center and maintains records of completion. Keeps abreast of new technology in the Auto Skills field and makes recommendations for change. Ensures control and accountability of inventory, supplies, and equipment. Ensures equipment and facilities meet all regulatory and safety standards and proper maintenance is performed on all equipment. Keeps work area clean, organized and in safety compliance. Initiates and follows up on maintenance trouble calls to get equipment/facility issues resolved. Ensures purchasing and pricing guidelines are adhered to in accordance with higher level instruction. Plans, organizes and carries out instructional classes. Ensures compliance with safety and environmental requirements in order to maintain a safe and healthful workplace. Submits mishap reports promptly and investigates all accidents. Transports patrons off-base to designated locations for trips, classes or programming. Monitors Auto Skills expenditures, account balances, and financial records. Provides supervisor with necessary figures for quarterly financial updates and the annual report. Uses varied and advanced functions of word processing to prepare, format, modify, edit, and print a variety of letters, memos, and other text documents. Promptly receives and transmits electronic messages with attachments and documents as appropriate.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes providing administrative assistance in support of a military unit or military activity in one or more of the following areas: Unit or individual training, medical readiness, personnel actions, financial actions, supply, or logistics; performing day-to-day administrative functions; and preparing or reviewing written products. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration, Strategic Management and Organizational Design and Development. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Administration and Management Fundamentals and Operations of Military and Civilian Pay Organizational Awareness Technical Competence

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the 377th Theater Sustainment Command, 855 Quartermaster Company, 766 Transportation Battalion, 643 Regional Support Group, 310 Expeditionary Sustainment Command located at Southbend, Indiana. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a Military Technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Manage the daily operations of a US Army Reserve unit's mission readiness program.
Represent the US Army Reserve Troop Program Unit Commander in his/her absence.
Perform as the record manager.
Serve as the unit physical security coordinator.
Review regulations and directives and implements changes in appropriate manner.
Compile data and create products to present at briefings.
Prepare and review command correspondence for content and accuracy.
Manage unit and individual personnel and medical readiness.
Execute the unit's supply and logistics program.
Coordinate the management of unit and individual training readiness.
Administer financial management program including Government Purchasing and Travel Card programs.
Advise on pay, benefits, entitlements, incentives, and assist with correcting pay issues.
Details.Education: FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. For further information, visit: http://www.ed.gov/about/offices/list/ous/international/usnei/us/edlite-visitus-forrecog.html

Veteran preference eligibles are listed ahead of non-preference eligibles within each quality category. Best Qualified. Candidates in this category possess exceptional skills and experience to exceed well above the minimum requirements for the announced position. Highly Qualified. Candidates in this category possess good skills and experience above the minimum requirements for the announced position. Qualified. Candidates in this category meet the minimum experience requirements for the announced position.

Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a PROGRAM ANALYST (TITLE 32), Position Description Number D1010000 and is part of the IL SMO, National Guard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: As a PROGRAM ANALYST (TITLE 32), GS-0343-7/9, you will serve as the analyst and consultant for the managementand administration of programs within the directorate or division. Major Duties - This is NOT an all-inclusive list: Review, evaluate and analyze obligations and expenditures. Summarize and interpret significant data collected and relate this data to the organizations program actions; identify and analyze deficiencies in resource consumption, training, workload and scheduling, and evaluate deviations from standards, plans, and estimates to determine cause and impact on missions. Assist management in interpretation and utilization of reports and information provided. Research and interpret personnel and training regulations, DA Pam's, Circulars and NGB guidance. Review trends and perform analysis of separate budget activities then provide information to management. Recommend funding allocations and monitors expenditure to ensure allocations are being utilized as planned and are not being exceeded. Verify that obligations and expenditures occur on a timely basis IAW current year program and monthly schedule of obligations and expenditures. Formulate and review all Annual Funding Guidance/Programs (AFG/AFP) ensuring obligation authority is not exceeded and budget adjustments are properly staffed. Provide recommendations to subordinate organizations for proper management of programs. Provide advice and assistance to management on accountability and legality of operating programs. Conduct training for proper management and accountability of programs. Aid functional areas in identifying areas of record documentation and procedures that can be streamlined, combined or improved and initiate methods to operate under the new or revised system. Advise management on timing of obligations and expenditures for Cooperative Agreement service contracts, equipment acquisitions and other unusual commitments. Develop various visual media to present trends, performance status, capability and related management information. Develop, collect, and maintain various historical data used to initiate planning, programming and execution of current and future training and operations programs. Monitor and track obligations and expenditures throughout the execution phase. Based on budget guidance received from higher headquarters, develop an annual budget for programs. Review prior and current budgets/funding trends, compile funding projections and prepare funding recommendations. Review daily and monthly funding documents to determine if updates are correct or require further action.

Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a VICE AIR COMMANDER (TITLE 32), Position Description Number D1469000 and is part of the IL 183 WG, National Guard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: As a VICE AIR COMMANDER (TITLE 32), GS-0340-14, you will provide leadership and management of the flying unit, to provide manpower, equipment, and training in peacetime, in preparation to perform the wartime mission. Major Duties - This is NOT an all-inclusive list: Assist in determining unit goals which are the foundation for long and short range planning and execution of all unit programs, and provide a focus for all unit functions and activities. Ensure goals coincide with national and state military strategies and local limitations. Consider factors such as current and future mission needs, political climate, environmental concerns, area demographics, and airfield and airspace operating conditions. Aid in developing the Base Land Use and Facilities Master Plan which is the key element in determining land and structure needs, facility siting, construction/modification, and future mission assignments. Ensure the development and implementation of a variety of federal, state and local programs to ensure mission effectiveness In conjunction with the Air Commander, negotiate and approve host/tenant agreements, memoranda of understanding, joint use and inter service agreements, leases, and licenses with military and civil agencies who provide and receive support, share resources, and interoperate with the unit. Develop Resource Protection Plan which identifies high value/risk assets, evaluate potential threats, and set levels of protection. Ensure a functional base information systems plan which provides for equipment/data security, communications, data processing, and audio/visual services. Assure timely identification of potential fleet integrity problems and notification of concerned major commands. Assist the Air Commander in ensuring the formulation, presentation, justification, and execution of an allocated multi-million dollar budget involving several major force elements and state funds. Serve on a broad range of committees and boards which formulate recommendations on policy, resource allocation, future planning, and provide feedback to leaders. Coordinate policies, plans, programs, and requirements at the senior leadership levels of the Air Force, Major Command, wartime gaining commands, National Guard Bureau, and the Adjutant General's Office. In conjunction with the Adjutant General's staff, and through subordinate staff members, plan, organize, direct, and control unit military and full-time personnel under several different personnel systems. Implement federal and state military and civilian Merit Promotion, Incentive Award, and Suggestion Programs. Ensure adequate training for all aspects of assigned tasks, and maintain an effective leadership/career development program. Ensure personnel are trained and exercised in their wartime skills.

Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a PROGRAM ANALYST (TITLE 32), Position Description Number D1905000 and is part of the IL USPFO, National Guard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: As a PROGRAM ANALYST (TITLE 32), GS-0343-7/9, you will provide management with objectively based information to effectively assess the full range of logistical asset accountability of all units/activities within the state. Major Duties - This is NOT an all-inclusive list: Develop sampling plans and procedures for validating unit/activity accountability and inventory certifications. Independently evaluate the effectiveness of substantive unit programs and processes in meeting their established goals and objectives. Analyze evaluation results on both a quantitative and qualitative basis to provide concise and objective information to identify accountability strengths and weaknesses. Develop recommendations to correct deficiencies or suggest program or process improvements for the organization. Recommend corrective action to re-establish and ensure unit/activity compliance, with applicable logistics and physical security regulations and directives, with a specified suspense date. Recommend internal reporting and status tracking procedures to ensure adequate control in terms of deadlines, progress reports, and follow-up reports. Plan, coordinate, and carry out the successive steps in fact-finding and analysis of issues necessary to complete each phase of assigned projects. Coordinate and/or conduct management studies of organization, staffing, work measurement, methods, or procedures. Apply statistical analysis techniques to measure progress, efficiency, and trends impacting the effectiveness of the organization to meet the organizational goals and objectives. Develop cost analysis of financial impact regarding accountability, equipment and supply damage, adequacy of storage, physical security and loss of federal supplies and equipment. Interpret a variety of requirements making independent judgments to determine organizational compliance with applicable regulations, procedures and practices. Develop processes, management, administrative, and technical evaluation plans for implementation by supervisors/managers.

Provide advice and assistance to management on accountability and legality of operating programs. Monitor and track obligations and expenditures throughout the execution phase. Investigate and prepare explanations of deviations from estimates or program objectives and develop recommendations to managers for budgetary adjustments.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: As a MEDICAL ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICER (Title 32), GS-0301-12, you will serve as the Senior Medical Officer for the entire installation, including tenant unit(s) and Geographically Separated Units (GSU) with responsibility for directing and managing all medical administrative functions including medical support, medical operations, force health management, force health protection, healthcare management, and related health applications. Major Duties - This is NOT an all-inclusive list: Implement the medical portion of the Designed Operational Capability (DOC) Statement of the unit. Develop and implement unit plans for execution of deployments In support of the USAF Air Expeditionary Force (AEF) requirements and contingency objectives to meet USAF and Joint Chief of Staff (JCS) goals. Direct work to be accomplished by the base medical and bioenvironmental programs, ensuring each is developed and implemented according to applicable regulations. Ensure compliance with all regulatory and legal requirements, medical readiness requirements, and the overall integrity of medical information and technology, force health management programs, and initiatives which operate to maintain and ensure a fit and ready force. Ensure compliance with all regulatory and legal requirements, medical readiness requirements, and the overall integrity of medical information and technology, force health management programs, and initiatives which operate to maintain and ensure a fit and ready force. Interpret, implement and administer laws, procedures, regulations and directives pertaining to various Air National Guard (Surgeon General or Medical) stand-alone, networked, or web-based medical systems including Preventative Health Assessment and Individual Medical Readiness (PIMR), Aerospace Services Information Management System (ASIMS), Aero medical Information Management Waiver Tracking System (AIMWTS), Grounding Management Information System (GMIS) Self-Inspection Database (SID), Central Credentials Quality Assurance System (CCQAS), Air Force Complete Immunization Tracking Application (AFCITA), Defense Occupational and Environmental Health Readiness System-Hearing Conservation (DOEHRS-HC), Environmental Management Information Systems (EMIS), Automated Civil Engineering System - Environmental Management (ACES-EM), or Enterprise Environmental Safety Occupational Health (EESOH) database, Command Core System (CCS), and Web-Based Integrated Tracking System (WBITS). Perspective and advice contribute substantially to management's ability to train and equip assigned personnel in light of dynamic and evolving medical environments. Represent and speak on behalf of the Wing Commander with regard to ANG Medical Management issues with representatives of the NGB, the Office of the Adjutant General/Joint State Headquarters, and other military components. Control utilization of health services program funds in collaboration with Medical Group Commander, Medical Group Executive Management Committee, Wing Commander, and Wing Comptroller. Ensure the installation maintains a strong viable human weapons system force fit for worldwide deployability. Collaborate with the Wing Commander and other senior management officials in the planning and development of short-term and long-term strategies for implementation of the Wing Strategic Plan. Attend staff meetings, formal briefings, and spontaneous informal sessions chaired or called by operations, unit deployments, exercises, and readiness or compliance inspections levied by USAF MAJCOM Inspector General's offices and other auditing agencies.

MajorDuties: As a FORCE INTEGRATION AND READINESS OFFICER (TITLE 32),GS-0301-9/11, you will serve as a primary staff member in the G3/5/7 with responsibility for force integration and readiness issues. Provide general direction on force integration actions through publication of the state long range Force Integration Plans which include evaluation of each planned action in terms of structure, personnel, equipment resources, training plans and facilities. Develop the state long range Force Integration Plan. Coordinate the development and update of Table of Distribution and Allowance (TDAs) and Modified Table of Organization and Equipment (MTOE). Analyze new authorization documents, identify conflicts, substantive changes and doctrinal issues, and recommend courses of action. Establish long term and near term milestones for force integration actions and ensure integration into the state training calendar.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: As a PROGRAM MANAGER (STRATEGIC PLANS AND POLICY OFFICER) (Title 32), GS-0340-12, you will serve as the Officer over Strategic Plans and Policy. Major Duties - This is NOT an all-inclusive list: Ensure standardized Interagency/Intergovernmental coordination processes with non-federalized (Title 32) National Guard across the state. Synchronize and integrate strategies with Combatant Commanders, National Guard Bureau (NGB), other services, supported federal and state agencies, and the federal response plan. Provide oversight on the coordination and administration of activities and programs which integrate military and non-military agencies and international programs as directed by NGB, Combatant Commanders (CoComs), Department of State, and other appropriate tasking authorities. Conduct and oversee the completion of detailed studies in response to the state Adjutant General and Chief Joint Staff requests and prepare executive summaries, information papers, and briefings for internal and external audiences. Provide support to: the Combatant Commanders Theater Security Coordination Plan; support for the Ambassador's Mission Performance Plan and Country Campaign Plan; and foreign liaison guidance and assistance to the Adjutant General, JFHQ-State, and subordinate elements. Provide oversight of state partnership programs and other international partnership activities. Employ advanced management principals, data compilations and the development of recommendations to affect current sources, infrastructure and future requirements. Provide direction and guidance to directors and staff in enhancement measurement tools and management improvement ideas. Evaluate and recommend planning strategies to develop, implement and sustain the Joint Force Headquarters Strategic Plan. Conduct statewide analysis for strategic planning, re-engineering issues, and program integration. Engage and work with strategic planners and functional management teams to ensure proper planning and analysis for future force structure activities including capabilities analysis, demographic information, and ongoing transformation planning for out-year activities. Review Department of Defense (DoD), Department of the Air Force, Department of the Army (DA), National Guard Bureau (NGB), Army National Guard (ARNG), Air National Guard (ANG), and other agency planning documents (i.e. National Military Strategy, Defense Planning Guidance, Quadrennial Defense Review, etc.) and ensure the state strategic plan remains synchronized with current topics, future initiatives and higher headquarters planning documents.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: MANDATORY QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: For this particular job, applicants must meet all competencies reflected under the Mandatory Qualification Criteria to include education (if required). Online resumes must demonstrate qualification by providing specific examples and associated results, in response to the announcement's mandatory criteria specified in this vacancy announcement: 1. Demonstrated experience advising senior leaders in the development and implementation of solutions and strategies, which address a wide range of management challenges. 2. Ability to collaborate with subject matter experts and/or stakeholders to meet end-strength, hiring, and position budget & change requirements. 3. Demonstrated communications skills to provide insight and explanations regarding common manpower inquiries (e.g. appropriate use of funding types; transfer; growth; decrements; overstrength; special hiring programs, and positions and authorities). 4. Experience recommending proactive position management strategies, which optimizes the use of existing manpower positions. 5. Experience briefing and engaging at events, forums, and/or working groups (internal and external) regarding manpower-related topics. EDUCATION REQUIREMENT: A. Education: Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Accounting, Business Administration, Business Management, Contract Management, Economics, Finance, Law, Political Science, Public Policy, or a related field. -OR- B. Combination of Education and Experience: A minimum of 24 semester (36 quarter) hours of coursework in any area listed in option A, plus experience in the provision of program management and oversight, policy and resource management, budget allocation and execution, or a related area that demonstrates the ability to successfully perform the duties associated with this work. As a rule, every 30 semester (45 quarter) hours of coursework is equivalent to one year of experience. Candidates should show that their combination of education and experience totals 4 years. -OR- C. Experience: A minimum of 4 years of experience in the provision of program management and oversight, policy and resource management, budget allocation and execution, or a related area that demonstrates the ability to successfully perform the duties associated with this work. DESIRABLE QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: In addition to the mandatory qualifications, experience in the following is desired: 1. Experience using and maintaining position tracking mechanisms and audit trails to account for positions and provide historical insights through standard coding and records. 2. Knowledge of Multi- Sector Workforce and full-time equivalent burn rates. 3. Extensive experience with utilizing and maintaining SharePoint sites.

Details.Requirements: SPECIAL INFO: As a condition of employment at NGA, persons being considered for employment must meet NGA fitness for employment standards. - U.S. Citizenship Required - Security Clearance (Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information) - Polygraph Test Required - Position Subject to Drug Testing - Two Year Probationary Period - Direct Deposit Required SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: You must be able to obtain and retain a Top Secret security clearance with access to Sensitive Compartmented Information. In addition, you are subject to a Counterintelligence Polygraph examination in order to maintain access to Top Secret information. All employees are subject to a periodic examination on a random basis in order to determine continued eligibility. Refusal to take the examination may result in denial of access to Top Secret information, SAP, and/or unescorted access to SCIFs. Employees with SCI access and who are under NGA cognizance are required to submit a Security Financial Disclosure Report, SF-714, on an annual basis in order to determine continued eligibility. Failure to comply may negatively impact continued access to Top Secret information, Information Systems, SAP, and/or unescorted access to SCIFs. NGA utilizes all processes and procedures of the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS). Non-executive NGA employees are assigned to five distinct pay bands based on the type and scope of work performed. The employee's base salary is established within their assigned pay band based on their unique qualifications. A performance pay process is conducted each year to determine a potential base pay salary increase and/or bonus. An employee's annual performance evaluation is a key factor in the performance pay process. Employees on term or temporary appointments are not eligible to apply for internal assignment opportunity notices. This position is a DCIPS position in the Excepted Service under 10 U.S.C. 1601. DoD Components with DCIPS positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 2005, DCIPS Employment and Placement. If you are an external applicant claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must self-identify your eligibility in our ERecruit application.

Discontinued service retirement annuitants (i.e., retired under section 8336(d)(1) or 8414(b)(1)(A) of title 5, United States Code) appointed to the Department of Defense may elect to be subject to retirement provisions of the new appointment as appropriate. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for a Management Analyst, your resume and supporting documentation must support: A. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position and is directly in or related to this position. To qualify at the GS-09 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements including time-in-grade (General Schedule (GS) positions only), time-after-competitive appointment, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut-off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: Analyzing and evaluating issues to identify, consider, and resolve problems of a procedural or factual nature. Providing administrative support for common workplace procedures, such as monitoring suspense, reporting, training support, telework management, employee surveys, and timekeeping. Utilizing procedures and regulations to ensure administrative submissions conform to requirements. Reviewing standard operating procedures and making recommendations to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of existing processes. B. Education Substitution: Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work. Education must be from a college or university accredited by an organization approved by the U.S. Department of Education. See http://ope.ed.gov/accreditation/Search.aspx. If using education to meet basic qualifications, YOU MUST SUBMIT A TRANSCRIPT as supplemental documentation. To qualify based on education in lieu of specialized experience, you must possess a master's or equivalent graduate degree OR two full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree OR LL.B. or J.D., if related.C. Combination: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements for grade level GS-09, and may be computed by first determining the applicant's total qualifying experience as a percentage of the experience required for the grade level; then determining the applicant's education as a percentage of the education required for the grade level; and then adding the two percentages. The total percentages must equal at least 100 percent to qualify an applicant for that grade level. Only graduate education in excess of the amount required for the next lower grade level may be used to qualify applicants for positions at grade GS-09. C. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Join Team DCMA -- Challenge yourself! They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. Report to the division chief and work daily with the command group in SOCEUR, the theater special operations command of USEUCOM.
Responsible for developing and executing the command?s strategic engagement strategy based on national level policy and guidance and CDR USEUCOM?s and CDR USSOCOM?s guidance.
Host strategic engagement working and planning groups and represent the strategic engagement division in internal meetings as well as with outside agencies.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions,attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, impressive gardens and parks, and palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles.It is the home to USAG Stuttgart, HQ US EUCOM, HQ US AFRICOM, and other tenant units. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. *COVID-19 has severely limited available child care services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities,host-nation child care providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with childcare requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process.* United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), is one of six U.S. Department of Defense' geographic combatant commands and is responsible to the Secretary of Defense for military relations with African nations, the African Union, and African regional security organizations. It is responsible for all DoD operations, exercises, and security cooperation on the African continent, its island nations, and surrounding waters. Its mission is to build defense capabilities, respond to crisis, and deter and defeat transnational threats in order to advance U.S. national interests and promote regional security, stability, and prosperity
MajorDuties: Establishes policies and procedures for accomplishing Counter Threat Finance (CTF) activities.
Identifies requirements and initiates requests for additional resources including personnel, equipment, and supplies to ensure success in meeting goals and objectives.
Develops theater-wide CTF intelligence collection plans, reporting guidance, and the organization of activities for the collection and dissemination of Threat Finance intelligence data.
Provides finance-specific analytical support to assist identifying, detecting, targeting and interdicting terrorist and/or illicit criminal activities.

Coordinates operational threat finance requirements with appropriate Combatant Commands, various U.S. Government and Non-Government Organizations, high-level officials from the banking industry and law enforcement agencies.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, impressive gardens and parks, and palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles. It is the home to USAG Stuttgart, HQ US EUCOM, HQ US AFRICOM, and other tenant units. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/
Details.SubAgencyName: United States Africa Command (US AFRICOM), J3
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. *COVID-19 has severely limited available child care services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation child care providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with child care requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process.* United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), is one of six U.S. Department of Defense' geographic combatant commands and is responsible to the Secretary of Defense for military relations with African nations, the African Union, and African regional security organizations. It is responsible for all DoD operations, exercises, and security cooperation on the African continent, its island nations, and surrounding waters. Its mission is to build defense capabilities, respond to crisis, and deter and defeat transnational threats in order to advance U.S. national interests and promote regional security, stability, and prosperity.
MajorDuties: Participate in all relevant USAFRICOM boards/centers/cells/working groups in the conduct of planning for crisis and contingency operations.
Contribute to cross-directorate teams that are responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing USAFRICOM activities and limited contingency response (LCR) operations.
Train and instruct staff on relevant fires and targeting topics.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as a Program Analyst (Institutional Capacity Building), GS-0343-13, located in ECJ5-SCP (Security Cooperation Programs) Division, Strategy, Plans and Policy, United States European Command (USEUCOM), in Stuttgart, Germany.
Details.SubAgencyName: HQ US EUROPEAN COMMAND J5/PLANS & POLICY DIRECTORATE
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/ Please note: COVID-19 has severely limited available childcare services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation childcare providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs.
MajorDuties: Provide subject matter expertise and analytical support in the institutional capacity building area/institution of security governance in order to inform security cooperation efforts with Partnership for Peace (PfP) countries.
Apply knowledge of US and NATO ICB objectives and priorities to the development and review of EUCOM Country (CPs) and other security cooperation planning efforts.
Identify gaps and overlaps in partner country reform efforts and make recommendations for deconflicting security cooperation programs.
Provide analytical and evaluative assistance to manage USEUCOM?s security cooperation programs. Prepare analyses with recommended actions.
Coordinate DOD contribution to broader, interagency security sector governance and security sector reform efforts to increase the sustainability of SC programs.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/ Please note: COVID-19 has severely limited available childcare services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation childcare providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs.
MajorDuties: Shape the development of the EUCOM perspective on global JEMSO policy by drafting and reviewing policy documents from the EUCOM staff, other CCMDs, and joint staff (JS).
Assist in the development of JEMSO aspects of tier one combatant command (CCMD) level exercise design.
Serve on operational planning teams (OPTs) developing JEMSO-related plans.
Plan, prepare and review point papers, talking papers, and briefings on JEMSO planning, strategy, and assessment matters related to this branch for EUCOM, as required.
Review work, accept or reject products and inputs.
Establish internal suspense and ensure all requirements/taskers are met in a timely manner.

Provide leadership, guidance, and supervision of joint military, civilian, and contractors within the division.
Maintain continuity across all branches of the director and ensure continuity of linkages with the intelligence, operations, and plans directorates.

GS-11 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Executing emergency action program procedures; 2) Transmitting emergency action messages; AND 3) Using secure emergency action communication systems for information flow. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Substitution of Education: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Political Science and Crisis/Emergency Management. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. GS-12 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Providing training to staff on emergency action procedures; 2) Communicating to a team to ensure an organization strategic plan/mission are integrated into a team's strategies/goals; AND 3) Drafting and transmitting Emergency Action Messages through both secure and unsecured communications systems. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11). NOTE: Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For GS-12, you must meet the qualification requirement as using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. NOTE: JCS/COCOM/JNOC experience highly desired. GS-12: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-11).

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. *COVID-19 has severely limited available child care services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation child care providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with child care requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process.* United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), is one of six U.S. Department of Defense' geographic combatant commands and is responsible to the Secretary of Defense for military relations with African nations, the African Union, and African regional security organizations. It is responsible for all DoD operations, exercises, and security cooperation on the African continent, its island nations, and surrounding waters. Its mission is to build defense capabilities, respond to crisis, and deter and defeat transnational threats in order to advance U.S. national interests and promote regional security, stability, and prosperity.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. *COVID-19 has severely limited available child care services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation child care providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with child care requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process.* Special Operations Command Africa (SOCAF) leads, plans, coordinates and, as directed, executes the full spectrum of Special Operations in US Africa Command's area of responsibility (AOR) as part of an integrated Theater Strategy to combat terrorism and advance US Africa Command's strategic objectives.
MajorDuties: Plan and execute deployment operations for all U.S. Special Operation Forces SOF throughout the USAFRICOM area of responsibility (AOR), and in support of other regional combatant commands around the world.
Participate in operations planning in either joint or operation planning groups.
Coordinate with SOCAFRICA J35 for the tracking of global force management (GFM) requirements and their associated JOPES sourcing data status.
Recommend contingency and crisis action with Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES) and Global Force Management (GFM) policies, procedures, products, and planning formulation.
Coordinate building of associated Time Phased Force Deployment Data (TPFDD) and Joint Capabilities Requirements Management (JCRM) files.
Utilize software applications such as Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES) or Rapid Query Tool (JET) to support deployment execution operations.
Analyze air transportation and surface (ground and/or sea) transportation of personnel and cargo to identify appropriate deployment and/or re-deployment modes of transportation requirements.
Present information on complex, time-sensitive force deployment management issues to brief senior leadership.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is responsible for all phases of international interoperability within the US European Command area of responsibility by integrating new technology, procedures, and training to answer Department of Defense (DoD/USEUCOM) theater security cooperation and U.S. embassy mission performance plan policy goals in theater.
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters United States European Command, J6 Cyber Directorate
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. For additional information please visithttps://home.army.mil/stuttgart/ Please note: COVID-19 has severely limited available childcare services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation childcare providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs.
MajorDuties: Serve as a primary US European Command interface to allied command transformation and allied command operations for improvement of interoperability.
Develop Multi-tactical data links (TADL) network (MTN) architectures in a joint and coalition environment based on joint force requirements and resolves connectivity and interoperability problems.
Develop, coordinates and conducts command and control interoperability boards (CCIBs) and other Command, Control, Communications, Computer (C4I) interoperability forums.

Technical expert in Multi-TADL network architectures and joint data network (JDN) systems including air defense situational indicator (ADSI), joint range extension (JRE) system and global command and control system-joint (GCCS-J) knowledge.
Develop Multi-TADL network architectures based on Joint Force industry requirements; to establish a Multi-TADL link structure and identify and document data and message traffic flow.

Coordinate policy, instructions, and doctrine for joint staff, National Security Agency (NSA), and US European Command regarding the international release of communications security (COMSEC)/cryptography within theater.
Coordinate and co-authors requests for exception to national disclosure policy (ENDP) regarding high end weapon platforms and airframes with embedded cryptography purchased by US allies in theater.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for providing support and analytical oversight of plans and policies associated with responsibilities for Deputy Directorate Joint Training (DDJT) entailing a broad range of complex, sensitive, and high-profile staff operations.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The Joint Staff assists the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff in accomplishing his responsibilities for: the unified strategic direction of the combatant forces; their operation under unified command; and for their integration into an efficient team of land, naval, and air forces. The Joint Staff is composed of approximately equal numbers of officers from the Army, Navy and Marine Corps, and Air Force. Joint Staff J-7, in support of the Chairman, trains, educates, develops, designs and adapts the globally integrated, partnered, joint force to achieve overmatch in the continuum of conflict under conditions of accelerating change in the character of war.
MajorDuties: As a PLANS & POLICY ANALYST at the GS-0301-12/13 some of your typical work assignments may include: A wide variety of significant organization wide projects and assignments, often with high visibility. Incumbent has delegated authority to initiate actions on policies and projects. Resolving problems and complex issues typically referred to DDJT Utilizing experience and sound judgement to achieve results in line with the organizations goals and objectives. Reviewing, analyzing, and evaluating DDJT plans and policies to ensure compatibility with higher headquarters, regulations, and guidance. Participating in DDJT and J-7 meetings to coordinate significant activities and long-range planning related to the Joint Training mission. Assessing organization's key decision-making/work processes identify actual or potential functional problems that relate to policy and planning efforts Providing technical direction for schedules, establishing agendas, and coordinating J-7 Flag/General Officer planning conferences and/or professional symposiums. Attending, participating in, and reporting status of cross divisional boards, bureaus, centers, cells, and working groups. Coordinating with personnel, internal and external to the organization, to resolve complex issues.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for providing support and analytical oversight of plans and policies associated with responsibilities for Deputy Directorate Joint Training (DDJT) entailing a broad range of complex, sensitive, and high-profile staff operations. .
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The Joint Staff assists the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff in accomplishing his responsibilities for: the unified strategic direction of the combatant forces; their operation under unified command; and for their integration into an efficient team of land, naval, and air forces. The Joint Staff is composed of approximately equal numbers of officers from the Army, Navy and Marine Corps, and Air Force. Joint Staff J-7, in support of the Chairman, trains, educates, develops, designs and adapts the globally integrated, partnered, joint force to achieve overmatch in the continuum of conflict under conditions of accelerating change in the character of war.
MajorDuties: As a PLANS & POLICY ANALYST at the GS-0301-12/13 some of your typical work assignments may include: Serves as the Operations Analyst for DDJT on a wide variety of significant organization wide projects and assignments, often with high visibility. Incumbent has delegated authority to initiate actions on policies and projects. Resolving problems and complex issues typically referred to DDJT Utilizing experience and sound judgement to achieve results in line with the organizations goals and objectives. Reviewing, analyzing, and evaluating DDJT plans and policies to ensure compatibility with higher headquarters, regulations, and guidance. Participating in DDJT and J-7 meetings to coordinate significant activities and long-range planning related to the Joint Training mission. Assessing organization's key decision-making/work processes identify actual or potential functional problems that relate to policy and planning efforts Providing technical direction for schedules, establishing agendas, and coordinating J-7 Flag/General Officer planning conferences and/or professional symposiums. Attending, participating in, and reporting status of cross divisional boards, bureaus, centers, cells, and working groups. Coordinating with personnel, internal and external to the organization, to resolve complex issues.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Responsible for leading the process to analyzing lessons observations from across the joint force, turning them into issues for resolution, and ensuring they are effectively incorporated into joint force development efforts. Analyzes all observations, issues, best practices and recommendations for uniqueness and completeness and puts them into the Joint Lessons Learned Information System (JLLIS) format for assignment.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: Joint Staff J-7, in support of the Chairman, trains, educates, develops, designs and adapts the globally integrated, partnered, joint force to achieve overmatch in the continuum of conflict in competition and crisis under conditions of accelerating change in the character of war.
MajorDuties: As a LESSONS LEARNED ANALYST at the GS-0301-13 some of your typical work assignments may include: Responsible for leading the process to analyze lessons observations from across the joint force, turning them into issues for resolution, and ensuring they are effectively incorporated into joint force development effort. Analyzes all observations, issues, best practices and recommendations for uniqueness, accuracy, relevance and completeness and puts them into the Joint Lessons Learned Information System (JLLIS) format for assignment, tracking and resolution. Collects, analyzes, documents, manage and integrate joint observations, best practices, and issue resolution, to advance the identification, validation, evaluation, institutionalization, and operationalization of joint lessons learned into Joint Force Development and Design. Develops, prepares, and processes products including, but not limited to, directives, information/decision papers, technical case studies, news brief releases, information flyers, brochures, reports, and inputs to reports. Monitors the development, modification, and integration of lessons learned processes, systems and equipment and ensures the integration of such changes into Joint Staff publications.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for developing and maintaining a comprehensive view of the future joint operating environment fifteen to twenty years into the future; developing threat based joint concepts that inform joint force development and design decisions; and developing concepts of operations (CONOPS) used to analyze new operational approaches and joint capability gaps.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: Joint Staff J-7, in support of the Chairman, trains, educates, develops, designs and adapts the globally integrated, partnered, joint force to achieve overmatch in the continuum of conflict in competition and crisis under conditions of accelerating change in the character of war.

Performs as a participant in a cross matrixed team with members across the DoD to write a joint concept (a written product) which provides the Joint Force with broad capabilities, attributes, and operational logic to address global challenges. Participates in core writing team working sessions, supports analysis of input from the cross matrixed team, and develops concept outlines, drafts, and final products based on synthesized core writing team input as well as other research and ensures that content and format adhere to the standards. Prepares and Produces decision briefings/ presentations at the general officer level to support investment decisions. Reviews, researches, develops and revises of Service, joint, and multi­national concepts; participating in pertinent seminars, meetings, workshops, conference, panels, working groups, assessments, studies, experiments, exercises, and wargames with involvement from Joint Staff, OSD, Services, Combatant Commands, Intelligence Community, Think Tanks, Multinational partners and Industry

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-09, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. (GS-09) One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service: Worked within a team to plan, coordinate, and execute protocol programs and events while adhering to protocol principles, methods, practices and precedence. Coordinated with individuals in regard to protocol in order to facilitate arrangements for site and facility selection, procurement of awards, press coverage, gift exchanges, appropriate menu selections, meetings, invitations, and seating arrangements. Served as a protocol escort for the duration of scheduled events while providing advice and assistance for unforeseen requirements and taking corrective action when a problem arose. OR B. (GS-09) Masters or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related (transcripts required for verification). OR C. (GS-09) You have some specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and you have more than one year but less than two years of education as described in B. You have computed the percentage of the requirements that you meet, and the total is at least 100%. (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of graduate education beyond the first year by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.) You may qualify at the GS-11, if you fulfill the following qualifications: D. (GS-11) I have 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-9) in the federal service: Applies the principles, methods, practices, and techniques associated with the execution of a protocol program, as well as a thorough knowledge of national and international rules, procedures, and forums prescribing traditional and diplomatic customs, courtesies, and etiquette: Conceptualizes, plans, coordinates, and executes high level military and civilian, foreign and domestic visits/functions, ceremonies and special events hosted by senior leadership; Plans and implements protocol for casual to formal social events. OR E. (GS-11) I possess one of the following: Ph.D. Or equivalent graduate degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related; OR F. (GS-11) You have some specialized experience as described in D, but less than one year; and you have more than one year but less than two years of education as described in E. You have computed the percentage of the requirements that you meet, and the total is at least 100%. (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of graduate education beyond the first year by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.) You may qualify at the GS-12, if you fulfill the following qualifications: G. (GS-12) One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service: Experience using the principles, methods, practices, and techniques associated with the execution of a protocol program, as well as a thorough knowledge of national and international rules, procedures, and forums prescribing traditional and diplomatic customs, courtesies, and etiquette: Conceptualizes, plans, coordinates, and executes high level military and civilian, foreign and domestic visits/functions, ceremonies and special events hosted by senior leadership; Plans and implements protocol for casual to formal social events. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for planning the execution of all protocol programs and providing the basis for the observance of correct protocol procedures and precedence for the Vice Director (O-8), SES Executive Director, Deputy Directors and senior staff regarding all protocol matters.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: Joint Staff J-7, in support of the Chairman, trains, educates, develops, designs and adapts the globally integrated, partnered, joint force to achieve overmatch in the continuum of conflict in competition and crisis under conditions of accelerating change in the character of war.
MajorDuties: As a PROTOCOL SPECIALIST at the GS-0301-9/11/12 some of your typical work assignments may include: Independently conceptualizes plans, coordinates and executes all protocol aspects of visits of high ranking US and foreign dignitaries and special ceremonies hosted by the Vice and Executive Director in honor of foreign delegations visiting the Joint Staff J7 and Joint Staff Directorates in Hampton Roads. Coordinates directly with appropriate individuals to facilitate arrangements for site and facility selection, procurement of awards, press coverage, gift exchanges appropriate menu selections, meetings, invitations, seating arrangements, etc Serves as protocol escort for the duration of the scheduled event, providing advice and assistance as required by the Vice Director for unforeseen requirements or taking corrective action that would allow the event to continue to a successful conclusion. Assistance provided must always exhibit total professionalism, tact, diplomacy and ensure a favorable impression. As a Protocol Specialist, identifies support requirements to stand-up and train exercise and other personnel in the successful management of the Joint Visitors Bureau (JVB)
Details.Education: ARE YOU USING YOUR EDUCATION TO QUALIFY? (APPLICABLE ONLY TO GS-09/GS-11 APPLICANTS) You MUST provide transcripts or other documentation to support your educational claims. All materials must be submitted by the closing date of the announcement. GRADUATE EDUCATION: One academic year of graduate education is considered to be the number of credits hours that your graduate school has determined to represent one academic year of full-time study. Such study may have been performed on a full-time or part-time basis. If you cannot obtain your graduate school's definition of one year of graduate study, 18 semester hours (or 27 quarter hours) should be considered as satisfying the requirement for one year of full-time graduate study. Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for reviewing the Secretary of Defense and Chairman's top future Joint Concepts, developing Concepts of Operations that apply the Joint Concepts against real-world operational problems, and designing the applications of the Concpt of Operations (CON OPS) into analytic activities such as wargames, Table­Top Exercises (TTX), and analytic studies.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: Joint Staff J-7, in support of the Chairman, trains, educates, develops, designs and adapts the globally integrated, partnered, joint force to achieve overmatch in the continuum of conflict in competition and crisis under conditions of accelerating change in the character of war.
MajorDuties: As a SUPERVISORY CONCEPT OF OPERATIONS BRANCH CHIEF at the GS-0301-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: Leads CONOPS development, leads Concepts of Employment (CONEMPS) development, performs oversight duties, supports concept development, supports wargaming efforts, and supports analysis efforts that require expert application of planning methods and a current knowledge of adversary threat trajectories Connects Joint Warfighting Concept ­related wargaming, experimentation, exercises, education, and research directly to the National Defense Strategy's approaches of integrated deterrence, campaigning, and building enduring advantages. Responsible for integrating CONOPS into myriad analytic efforts, such as wargames, TTXs, and analytic studies. Develops and maintains a repository of ideas, articles, studies, reports and other documents from across the joint warfighting development community for possible inclusion into joint concept development activities. Applies knowledge, expertise, and assessment of adversary methods of warfighting, capability trends and trajectories, joint warfighting operations and operational assessments; identifying and integrating related projects or initiatives; identifying issues in need of remediation.
